classification.difficultyReason: Apply the named vertical line test to the solid curves, then read their horizontal and vertical extents from turning points, filled endpoints and arrows.

content.prompt: Use the vertical line test to find which of the following graphs represent functions.

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex (1,-1), zeros 0 and 2, arrows at both upper ends, labelled axes and source ticks; no grid.
spec.mathematics: Curve y=(x-1)^2-1, inferred uniquely from the supplied parabola features.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied relation is always visible; classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the parabola at most once, so each input has only one output. It is a function.

spec.description: Major lower circular arc from (-6,8) to (6,8), closed endpoints, extrema x=±10 and y=-10. Dashed horizontal endpoint-height guide at y=8 is separate from the relation. No grid.

spec.answerVisibility: Only the source relation and its dashed guide are visible in the question.

answer.worked: A vertical line near either side of the circle meets the solid arc twice. One input therefore has two outputs, so the relation is not a function. The dashed line is a guide, not part of the relation.

spec.description: Increasing straight line through (0,-1) and (2,0), arrowheads at both ends; source ticks 2 on x and -1 on y. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied line is visible; no test line or answer is supplied.

answer.worked: Every vertical line meets the sloping straight line exactly once. It passes the vertical line test and is a function.

spec.description: Right-opening parabola with vertex (-1,0), passing through (0,1) and (0,-1); arrows at both rightward ends. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; classification and witness points are answer content.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=0$ meets the graph at $(0,1)$ and $(0,-1)$. The same input has two outputs, so the relation is not a function.

spec.description: Bounded sideways oscillating curve with closed endpoints (2,3) and (2,-3), two left turns at x=-2 and a middle right turn at (2,0). Unlabelled intermediate heights are schematic, not additional numerical givens. No grid.

spec.answerVisibility: All source features are permanent givens; no vertical test line is printed.

answer.worked: The vertical line $x=0$ meets the curve more than once. The relation fails the vertical line test, so it is not a function.

answer.worked: Although the curve changes direction, every vertical line meets it at most once. It passes the vertical line test and is a function.
